protocol_and_schema_notes.rules_pdf_version: SEPVAL Challenge Events and Rules of Participation, v4
protocol_and_schema_notes.rules_pdf_statement: The rules document describes 30 SEP events selected between 2011-2023 and 33 non-event periods selected between 2012-2023; both sets span Solar Cycles 24 and 25 and include difficult flare/CME-associated quiet periods.
protocol_and_schema_notes.inputs_and_triggers: Flare X-ray information, active region, M2M/CDAW/CACTUS CME parameters, DONKI links, and proton-response context are supplied with the challenge lists.
protocol_and_schema_notes.regular_cadence_issue_window: Start 24 hours before flare peak and continue until SEP peak, or until 14 hours after flare peak for a non-event.
protocol_and_schema_notes.causal_rule: Use only inputs/triggers available before the observed quantity; flare peak and CME start/eruption times are the relevant trigger times.
protocol_and_schema_notes.issue_time_rule: Estimate issue time from the last input used plus model processing time; for M2M CME parameters use the latest last-SOHO/last-STEREO image timestamp plus 15 minutes before adding computation time.
protocol_and_schema_notes.output_format: CCMC SEP Scoreboard JSON; include last-input and trigger timestamps, input identities, and a training-inclusion Boolean.
event_fields: >10, >100, >30 and >50 MeV start and peak times

source_version.commit_subject: Fix bug in paths output to SEP lists

algorithm_and_schema_notes.idsep: Estimates mean background and sigma over a time series; points above mean + 3 sigma are treated as enhancements by default, with configurable windows.
algorithm_and_schema_notes.opsep: Analyzes individual events and applies operational definitions >10 MeV at 10 pfu and >100 MeV at 1 pfu by default; supports additional thresholds and background-derived thresholds.
algorithm_and_schema_notes.time_type: Python datetime/pandas timestamps; public examples and CLEAR lists use ISO-like UTC timestamps.
algorithm_and_schema_notes.output: CSV event summaries plus CCMC SEP Scoreboard JSON; JSON can include issue time, model metadata, triggers, prediction windows, energy channel, species, location, peak intensity/time, event length, threshold crossings, all-clear, and profile paths.
algorithm_and_schema_notes.quality_note: The CLEAR documentation marks onset peak as an experimental, automatically identified field; treat onset target quality separately from operational threshold labels.
